title: Weights and Measures Regulation 35/1997
text:
LEGAL NOTICE NUMBER 35/1997
WEIGHTS AND MEASURES REGULATIONS
1. Issuing Authority
These regulations are issued by the Minister of Trade (commerce) and Industry,
pursuant to the authority vested in him by Article 18 of the Eritrean Standards
Institution Proclamation No.75 of 1995, (hereinafter referred to as the
"Proclamation.")
2. Short Title
These regulations may be cited as the "Weights and Measures Regulations, Legal
Notice No.35/1997”
3. Definitions
The terms defined in Article 2 of the Proclamation shall apply
In these regulations unless the context otherwise requires:
(1) "Inspector" shall mean any person authorized by the General Manager of the
Institution to perform the duties of an Inspector under Article 6 of these
regulations.
(2) "Seller of measuring instruments" shall mean any person who professionally
and/or for gain sells or otherwise transfers measuring instruments to users.
(3) "User" shall mean any person who uses a measuring instrument for the
purpose of trade and commerce, for fixing values for customs and transport
charges and for safety and health, but shall not include a person using a
measuring instrument for domestic use.
(4) "Reference Standard" shall mean a standard of the highest meteorological
quality available at a given location from which measurements made at
location are derived.
(5) "Working Standard" shall mean a measurement standard which, usually
calibrated against a Reference Standard, is used routinely to inspect and verify
measuring instruments.
(6) "Inspection" shall mean the process of checking a measuring instrument by an
inspector for compliance concerning accuracy and other requirements with
relevant Eritrean Standard or regulations.
(7)" Verification" shall mean the marking of a measuring instrument with the
standards mark by an inspector after he has inspected the measuring
instrument and found it to be accurate and in compliance with the relevant
Eritrean Standards or regulations.

4. Initial Inspection and Verification
No manufacturer, importer or seller of measuring instruments shall sell or
otherwise transfer measuring instruments to a user unless such measuring
instruments have been inspected and verified by an inspector in accordance with
Article 12 and 13 of these regulations.
5. Designation of Inspectors
The Institution shall designate Inspectors with appropriate identification cards for
the purpose of inspection and verification of measuring instruments.
6. Duties of Inspectors
(1) An Inspector at such time or within such periods of time as may be prescribed
within the regulation shall inspect and verify every measuring instrument that
are used or hold in possession for use by a user.
(2) An Inspector may at any reasonable time enter any shop, store, warehouse or
any other place where he has reason to believe that products are bought, sold,
exposed or kept for sale.
(3) An Inspector may seize and detain any measuring instrument which appears to
him to have been in use in contravention with the provisions of this regulation
and shall issue an official receipt to the user.
(4) An Inspector shall maintain a record of verifications of measuring instruments
carried out by him in which shall be recorded the names, addresses of the users
of the measuring instruments verified, the dates of such verifications and a
description of the types and number of measuring instruments so verified and
he shall sign each entry with respect to each user.
7. Duties of Dealers in Measuring Instruments
(1) Every manufacturer, importer and seller of measuring instruments shall keep a
written record of all sales or transfers of measuring instruments.
(2) Every manufacturer, importer or seller of measuring instruments shall file with
the Institution within seven days statements of all measuring instruments
possessed, sold or transferred during the previous three months.
8. Notice of Inspection and Verification
(1) The Institution shall publish, as it deems fit a notice in a newspaper of general
circulation specifying the locality within which users must have their measuring
instruments inspected and verified and the dates between which and the place
where an inspector will be available to carry out such inspection and
verification.
(2) Not later than the period specified by the Institution in the notice published
under the provisions of Sub-Article (1) of this Article, each user within the
specified locality or localities shall apply to an Inspector for inspection and
verification of his measuring instruments, specifying the number and nature of
the measuring instruments in his possession.

9. Defaulting Users of Measuring Instruments
(1) If after the expiry of any period specified by the Institution pursuant to sub-
Article (1) of Article 8 of this regulation, an Inspector discovers any unverified
measuring instrument in use in the specified locality or localities, he shall forbid
the use of the measuring instrument until it has been verified in accordance with
this regulation and shall report such action to the Institution which may initiate
any criminal suit.
(2) Any measuring instrument found by an Inspector in any place where
commercial transactions are carried out shall be deemed to be in use for the
purpose of such commercial transactions.
10. Duties of Users
(1) A user submitting a measuring instrument for verification shall:
(a) present the instrument in a clean condition;
(b) prepare the instrument so that the Inspector may examine the different
parts; and
(c) provide sufficient labour for the prompt and proper handling of any
material to be used in the verification of the measuring instrument.
(2) No person shall alter, obliterate, detach any seal, stamp or mark affixed,
attached or impressed upon any measuring instrument without the written
consent of the Inspector.
(3) No user shall hide fact or refuse to produce and exhibit for verification any
measuring instrument, which is subject to inspection upon demand being made
by an Inspector.
(4) No person shall obstruct, hinder or molest an Inspector in the performance of
his duties.
(5) If, at any time after the verification of a measuring instrument, a defect should
occur causing such measuring instrument to become inaccurate, the user shall
immediately report its condition to the Inspector so that it may be repaired
inspected and re-verified.
11. Verification Standards
(1) Working Standards shall be used at all times when an Inspector verifies
measuring instruments.
(2) If any user challenges the correctness of the Working Standards, Reference
Standards maintained by the Institution shall be the conclusive evidence in all
disputes.

12. Results of Inspection
(1) If on inspection a measuring instrument is found to be accurate, the Inspector
shall proceed in accordance with the provisions of Article 13 of these
regulations.
(2) The inspector shall require the user of a measuring instrument which is found
on inspection to be inaccurate to rectify the inaccuracy within a reasonable
period of time specified by him and shall forbid the use of such inaccurate
measuring instrument by sealing or by stamping in such manner as to indicate
that it is inaccurate or by sticking a notice on such inaccurate measuring
instrument declaring it to be unfit for use, as the case may be.
(3) The user of the measuring instrument shall ask the permission of the
inspector, within the specified period, to remove the seal, stamp or notice
attached to the measuring instrument for the purpose of adjusting the
inaccuracy. The inspector shall immediately grant permission by removing
the seal; stamp or notice attached to such measuring instrument and after it has
been adjusted found it to be accurate shall then verify the measuring
instrument in accordance with the provisions of Article 13 of these
regulations.
(4) If however, after the specified period, the inaccuracy has not been rectified
and the inspector discovers that the inaccurate measuring instrument is being
used he shall seize the inaccurate measuring instrument and submit a report to
this effect to the Institution.
13. Verification of Measuring Instruments
(1) On satisfaction that:
(a) the user of a measuring instrument has paid the appropriate fee prescribed in
Schedule 1 of this regulation; and
(b) the measuring instrument complies with the relevant Eritrean Standards or
regulations.
The inspector shall verify the measuring instrument by labelling it or marking it
in the appropriate place with Standards Mark established by the Institution.
(2) The year of verification may also be indicated marking the measuring
instrument with the last two figures of the European calendar year enclosed
within a circle.
14. Re-verification of Measuring Instruments
(1) The Institution shall cause all verified measuring instruments to be inspected
and re-verified regularly, the period depending upon the type and frequency of
use of the measuring instrument.

(2) The Institution may arrange at any time for surprise visits by an Inspector to
premises where measuring instruments are in commercial use or fixing values
for customs charge, in transport charges or in activities related to safety and
health.
(3) If, on re-verification, a measuring instrument is found to be inaccurate, the
Inspector shall obliterate all previous labels or marks of verification and shall
proceed in accordance with the provisions of sub-Articles (2) and (3) of
Article 12 of these regulations.
15. Certificate of Verifications
When a measuring instrument has been verified the Inspector shall at the request
of the user of such measuring issue a certificate of verification in the form
prescribed in Schedule II of these regulations.
16. Fees
(1) at the time of:
(a) initial verification of measuring instruments under the provisions of Article 4
of these regulations the importer, manufacturer or seller of the measuring
instrument shall pay;
(b) inspection and verification of a measuring instrument the user of such
measuring instrument shall pay; the fees prescribed in Schedule 1 of these
regulations for each measuring instrument inspected and verified.
(2) An official receipt shall be issued for all fees received by the Inspector.
17. Penalty
Any person who contravenes the provisions of these regulations shall be punished
in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Penal Code.
18. Effective Date
These regulations shall come into force on the date of their publication in the
Gazette of Eritrean Laws.
Done at Asmara, this 15th day of December, 1997
Aliseid Abdela
Minister of Trade and Industry
